title: await_sandbox_verdict is inert; only observable effect is a 30s stall
detail: Both angles independently found ITEM-3's readiness wait cannot change any verdict: the sweep skips every run_in_sandbox row before probing, and should_sandbox() requires run_in_sandbox, so no probed row consults sandbox state. The correctness angle MEASURED a 30.11s lib-test run caused entirely by SANDBOX_READY_TIMEOUT. I had seen 30.13s in my own earlier run and not questioned it.
resolution: Removed the wait, both consts, await_verdict_with and its three unit tests. The skip IS the ordering guarantee and is structural rather than timing-dependent, which is strictly stronger than a timed wait; the module doc now makes that argument explicitly. Measured: the boot_probe integration suite went from 32.62s to 2.52s.

title: TEST-1/TEST-6 'untested' assertion is satisfied by the column DEFAULT
detail: mcp_servers.last_health_check_status DEFAULTs to 'untested' and the create path writes no health record for a sandboxed row, so deleting the skip's record_health_check_on outright would still pass. The assertion could not distinguish 'recorded untested' from 'never touched the row' — the third vacuous-test finding on this workstream.
resolution: Both tests now seed a stale 'unhealthy' verdict + reason before the act, and additionally assert the stale reason was REPLACED and the new reason is non-empty. The assertion now proves a write.

title: not_testable computed independently of the branch actually taken
detail: not_testable was derived from existing.run_in_sandbox alone while the is_built_in arm is evaluated first, so a row that were both would have a genuine probe failure filed as 'untested'. Unreachable today (no built-in sets run_in_sandbox) but the guard and the branch encoded different predicates.
resolution: The flag is now SET BY the branch that runs (`not_testable = true` inside the sandboxed arm), so the two cannot diverge.

title: Doc comments orphaned by the auto-disable removal
detail: mcp/mod.rs spawn site still promised 'auto-disable unreachable ones'; events.rs named the boot check as an AutoDisabled emitter twice; connection_health.rs described 'list / record / disable' through the passed pool and 'a boot-time auto-disable is visible next time'.
resolution: All six sites rewritten to the actual post-change control flow.

title: Two functions' doc comments merged onto one
detail: The prose written for sandboxed_server_not_testable had no separator before health_record_for's own doc, so it attached to the wrong function and sandboxed_server_not_testable shipped undocumented.
resolution: Doc block moved onto the function it describes.

title: Test Connection is neutralised for a whole class, and the UI still paints it red
detail: sandboxed_server_not_testable keeps success:false, and BOTH UI call sites map success===false to message.error(). A user gets a red error toast whose own body reads 'This is a limit of the test, NOT a problem with the server.' I fixed the badge tooltips in DRIFT-1 and missed the toasts — the same defect one layer up. Verified by reading handleTest and handleSaveAndTest.
resolution: Both toast sites now branch on the row's own run_in_sandbox (already present client-side, so no public API field was added) and use message.info with the backend's explanation.

title: Sandbox guard bypassed when `existing` fails to resolve; health write was unscoped
detail: not_testable and the sandboxed arm key off `existing` (loaded via the ownership- and is_system=false-scoped lookup), but the health write used request.id unscoped. So POSTing a SYSTEM sandboxed row's id to the USER route resolves existing=None, probes on the host, and stamps that system row 'unhealthy' with the verbatim host-allowlist message — re-creating on the system row the exact badge and wording this change removes. The unscoped write pre-dates the diff; what is new is that INV-2 was claimed while holding only on the resolved path.
resolution: Both routes now gate the health write on the SCOPED lookup (`existing.as_ref().map(|s| s.id)`) rather than request.id.

title: Persisted-vocabulary contract in models.rs is now false; generated artifacts stale
detail: The doc said 'Defaults to untested for freshly-created rows that have never been probed' and 'reason: None on healthy / untested' — both false once a declined probe writes untested WITH a reason and a fresh timestamp. Those doc strings are the source of 8 locations across both workspaces' openapi.json + types.ts.
resolution: Source doc corrected, and all four generated artifacts patched to match. A full regen was attempted and REVERTED: this worktree's config has js_tool and voice disabled, so regenerating deleted 3,845 lines belonging to another worker's in-flight feature-surface reduction. The surgical patch was verified by the repo's own golden oracle (openapi::tests::types_ts_parity + _desktop), which was itself proven non-vacuous by introducing a one-word mismatch and observing it go RED.

title: New error code duplicates an existing one for the identical predicate
detail: SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE/400 was introduced for `get_state().is_none()`, which user_policy::enforce::require_sandbox_state already answers with MCP_SANDBOX_DISABLED/422. Two codes and two statuses for one condition, and 400 blames the client for a deployment-side absence.
resolution: Aligned to MCP_SANDBOX_DISABLED + unprocessable_entity. Free to do because the branch is new — nothing ever returned the other code.

title: Test registration broke the file's comment-after-mod convention
detail: The leading comment landed between `mod runtime;` and a pre-existing comment, retargeting that comment onto the new module.
resolution: Comment moved after the mod line, matching the file.

title: 'unhealthy' is now unreachable for sandboxed rows, and EVERY user stdio server is sandboxed
detail: Verified independently: user_policy/enforce.rs:56 and :85 force run_in_sandbox=Some(true) on every user stdio server, on create AND on every update. So the skip's blast radius is the whole user-stdio class, not just the Rscript case. All four health writers now skip or write 'untested' for that class, so no probe path can ever mark one unhealthy.
resolution: ACCEPTED, not fixed — and stated plainly in the PR rather than left implicit. Before this change that class did get a verdict, but it was a WRONG verdict produced by host-probing a guest-only command; removing a wrong signal is not removing a correct one. There is genuinely no probe path that can validate a sandboxed server today, and inventing one (a sandbox-capable Test Connection) is DEC-4's recorded follow-up. Escalated to the owner as the honest cost of the fix.

title: Auto-disable removal costs a re-dial per chat turn for genuinely dead non-sandboxed servers
detail: Tool collection iterates accessible servers in a sequential loop gated only on `enabled`. A permanently dead enabled server previously dropped out at the next restart; now it is re-dialled every chat request, and the stdio connect path has no handshake timeout (timeout_seconds is only honoured in client/http.rs).
resolution: ACCEPTED. The owner's brief explicitly required that 'a probe failure must not silently DISABLE an admin's server on boot', so ITEM-2 is a requested behaviour change, not an invention. The cost the auditor identifies is real and is now stated in the PR body and DEC-2 so the owner decides with it in view. The missing stdio handshake timeout is pre-existing and out of scope.

title: llm_repository solved this exact problem with a NEW status value, not by overloading 'untested'
detail: The sibling module added `unverified` with a CHECK-constraint migration, an API enum, and a distinct UI treatment, with the comment 'a state that is invisible in the UI is a state the operator reads as healthy'. This change overloads 'untested' and encodes the distinction only as 'reason is non-null', so the two meanings share a tag, tone, text and data-testid.
resolution: ACCEPTED as a follow-up, not adopted here. Matching it means a migration, a public enum, an OpenAPI regen for both workspaces and a UI treatment — which would also take the branch out of LIGHT tier. Recorded as the better long-term shape, with the precedent named so the follow-up does not have to rediscover it.

title: The two boot sweeps now behave oppositely for the same event
detail: llm_repository's boot sweep still calls disable_for_health_failure and documents itself as mirroring 'the MCP module's startup probe pattern'. After this change the same admin, on one restart, sees an unreachable LLM repository disabled and an unreachable MCP server not.
resolution: ACCEPTED, out of scope — changing another module's boot behaviour is a separate decision with its own review. Named in the PR body so the owner sees the divergence rather than discovering it, and so whoever resolves it does so deliberately in one direction.

title: Neither UI change has automated coverage
detail: The two tooltip branches and the two toast branches change behaviour with no spec touched; data-testid=mcp-health-untested appears nowhere under ui/tests.
resolution: ACCEPTED and stated rather than papered over. Covering it means an E2E that stands up a sandboxed stdio row, which needs a code_sandbox-enabled deployment and a rootfs — disproportionate here. Recorded in TESTS.md as a known coverage gap.

title: await_verdict_is_bounded_when_the_status_never_settles proved less than it claimed
detail: Timeout 150ms, assertion elapsed < 5s — an implementation ignoring the deadline entirely would pass.
resolution: Obsolete: the test was deleted with the mechanism it covered (F-1).
